title: Splendor-Online (Nova Frontier Online)
tagline: Online multiplayer adaptation of a gem-trading board game, reskinned as a space setting; an Express and WebSocket server holds the state.
summary: The repo's CLAUDE.md calls it a full-stack multiplayer Splendor board game; the player-facing name in README and metadata is Nova Frontier Online. A React 19 and Vite client talks over WebSocket to one large server.ts that validates actions, runs bot turns and a turn timer, and snapshots state to a JSON file. Docs describe six expansion modes, a manual playtest checklist and an acceptance matrix with one combo phase still pending. Bot commentary can call the Gemini API.

aiRole.summary: CLAUDE.md is a guidance file for Claude Code (E16) and AGENTS.md is a repository-guidelines file for coding agents (E17); the README opens with the Google AI Studio export template (E13) and metadata.json declares a server-side Gemini API capability (E14). At runtime the server can ask Gemini for bot commentary (E15, E18). The repo records no review of agent-written code beyond its own checklists, and no run results.

claims.text: The server checks game actions itself. A game_action is refused unless the sender is the active player, and other actions are refused while a cargo-limit discard is owed. For buy_card it finds the card in server-held state, checks Special Tech ownership and canBuyCard, then saves an undo snapshot before executing.

Rule logic is in src/utils/nova-frontier-rules.ts, imported by server.ts and tested by a Vitest file beside it; AGENTS.md tells contributors to keep rule-heavy logic there rather than in components. Tests were not run for this entry.

Server state is snapshotted to a JSON file (path from NOVA_STATE_FILE, with a backup path and cleanup of finished rooms after 1 hour and empty waiting rooms after 30 minutes), and a manual guide describes restart-and-reconnect checks.

excerpts.title: buy_card is resolved and validated on the server
excerpts.why: The client sends only a cardId. The server looks the card up in the player's reserved cards or the board, rejects unknown cards, checks the Special Tech is owned and unused, runs the shared canBuyCard rule, and only then stores an undo snapshot and mutates state.

excerpts.title: Snapshot file and retention settings
excerpts.why: Persistence is on unless NOVA_STATE_PERSISTENCE is 'off'. The snapshot path and a derived backup path are configurable, and finished and empty rooms expire on fixed timers.

demo.note: Runs locally (npm run dev per the README). The README links an AI Studio app page, which is not a documented public deployment and was not checked.

limitations: Docs disagree with the code: CLAUDE.md says there is no database and names src/utils/splendor-rules.ts (E5), but the tree has server/statePersistence.ts (E6) and the rules live in nova-frontier-rules.ts. AGENTS.md says no test framework is configured (E8) while package.json runs vitest (E9) and test files exist (E10).

The acceptance matrix marks the standalone expansions passed, but those ticks are the repo's own manual statements. Combo Phase 3 is still 'Code Enabled, Pending Full Manual Validation' (E11), and the playtest checklist items are unchecked (E12). No playtest result or player feedback is recorded.
Nothing was run for this entry (type-check, Vitest, server); no CI results are in the repo.

The game is an adaptation of a commercial board game, renamed in the UI by rule (E7). Card and city artwork under public/images was not examined, and its provenance is not recorded here, so no images are shown.
Most server logic is in one 3,483-line server.ts, and a runtime state snapshot file under .data/ is committed; neither was reviewed beyond the cited lines.
contribution: All 130 commits are attributed to the owner's account, 2026-06-05 to 2026-06-21. No other contributors.
